subtype: Approach: dividing jobs by what each person is good at [Action]
passage: Thursday. Group project day! Our chart is on the water cycle. At first we all wanted to do the same fun bits. Then I said, why don't we give each person the job they like best? Meera loves drawing, so she does the pictures. Aman writes neatly, so he does the sentences. Riya likes cutting and pasting, so she gets the scissors. Karan speaks well, so he will present. I checked facts and helped everyone. Nobody argued even once. We finished before the bell, and Meera's rain clouds look better than anything I could draw. Manjula.

qa.q: Who is going to present the chart?
Why do you think Manjula is pleased at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Manjula is pleased because the jobs matched what people like, nobody argued, and the chart finished before the bell. 😊

qa.q: What alternative approach could the group use if a member falls behind, and why?
qa.a: The group could check in halfway and let others share the slow job. Then the chart would still be ready on time.

qa.q: How might Meera see her job in the group?
qa.a: Meera got to do the drawing she loves, so the pictures probably feel like a real contribution, and the praise for the clouds shows the group values it.

grounding: The group assigns drawing, writing, cutting and presenting by what each member is good at, so the work moves faster with less quarrelling.

subtype: Approach: dividing jobs by what each person is good at [Action]
passage: The Class 6 project at the kasba school was a big chart on 'Crops of Our District', and last time the group had fought for three days. This time Lalit said, "Let's do what each of us is best at." Shankar drew the best; everyone knew his bullock-cart pictures. So Shankar drew the fields. Lalit had the neatest handwriting, so he wrote the captions. Geeta loved cutting and pasting, and brought seeds of wheat, mustard and gram to stick on. Munni, who was never scared in front of the class, would present it. Nobody fought over the glue this time. The chart was done in two afternoons, and Munni's talk made Masterji clap.

qa.q: How might Shankar have felt being given the drawing?
qa.a: He likely felt proud and happy, since everyone knew his bullock-cart pictures were the best.

qa.q: What could the group do if two people want the same job?
qa.a: Share it, or let one take it this time and the other next time; matching jobs to skills is what made the work fast and calm.

qa.q: How might Masterji see the finished chart?
qa.a: Masterji clapped at Munni's talk, so Masterji seems pleased with a chart done quickly and well.

grounding: Shows a group giving each member the job they are best at, drawing, writing, pasting and presenting, so the work goes faster with less quarrelling.

subtype: Approach: dividing jobs by what each person is good at [Action]
passage: In Montevideo, Camila's group had a week to make a poster about the birds of their city park. The first meeting turned into an argument over who would hold the markers. At the second, Camila tried something else. "What's everyone best at?" Vera drew birds all over her notebooks, so she took the drawings. Camila liked writing and took the facts. Lucas was good with scissors and glue. Mateo, who loved talking, would present. After that, each worked on their own part at the same table, passing things along. The poster was finished by Wednesday, two days early, and Vera's hummingbird was so good that the teacher pinned it by the door.

qa.q: Whose drawing did the teacher pin by the door?
How might Camila have felt after the first meeting?
qa.a: She probably felt frustrated by the argument over markers, which pushed her to try a different way.

qa.q: Why did dividing jobs by skill speed things up?
qa.a: Each person worked on what they enjoyed and were good at, so there was less quarrelling and the poster was done two days early.

qa.q: How might Mateo see his job?
qa.a: Mateo loves talking, so presenting likely feels like a fun job rather than a chore.

grounding: Illustrates a group dividing a project by what each member does best, which speeds up the work and cuts down on quarrels.
